title: ALDER YARD — Shade and outdoor learning for a school courtyard, 14 deliverables

config.text:
# ALDER YARD

## Project
- School courtyard for outdoor lessons and breaks
- Climate context: hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters
- Site boundary: 40 m east-west by 30 m north-south
- Total site area: 1,200 m²
- Existing building footprint: 192 m²
- Landscape area: 1,008 m²
- Existing building appearance: cream brickwork, teal window frames, flat parapet
- Existing building height: 6,000 mm
- South ground level: +0 mm
- North ground level: +300 mm
- Ground gradient: uniform 1% rise toward north
- East maintenance passage: 4 m clear width
- Learning route from D1: maximum 35 m walking distance; minimum 1.8 m clear width

## Use and shade
- Class: 30 pupils and one teacher
- Learning furniture: six five-pupil tables and one teacher position
- Break: 60 pupils; 30 in Assembly Court and 30 in Open Lawn
- Assembly Court: 120 m²
- Assembly Court geometric shade target: at least 90 m² at 12:30 on 15 July
- Shade structure footprint envelope: 12 m by 10 m, coincident with Assembly Court
- Shade structure minimum clear height: 3,000 mm
- Shade structure maximum overall height: 4,500 mm
- Shade methods: overhead canopy and grouped trees
- Planting layers: trees, shrubs and groundcover
- Water Court surface: 120 m² permeable concrete

## Zone areas
| Zone | Area |
|---|---:|
| Assembly Court | 120 m² |
| Learning Terrace | 120 m² |
| Grove | 180 m² |
| Open Lawn | 140 m² |
| Water Court | 120 m² |
| Circulation | 328 m² |

## Plant palette
| Code | Plant name | Quantity | Role |
|---|---|---:|---|
| CA | Celtis australis | 4 retained + 2 new | Tree canopy |
| MT | Myrtus communis 'Tarentina' | 24 | Shrub layer |
| CD | Carex divulsa | 120 | Groundcover layer |

## Printed wording
- Site name: ALDER YARD
- Shade drawing title: Geometric shade study
- Scene labels: 09:30 lesson; 12:30 break
- Zone names: Assembly Court; Learning Terrace; Grove; Open Lawn; Water Court; Circulation
- Plant names: Celtis australis; Myrtus communis 'Tarentina'; Carex divulsa

## Surface palette
- Assembly Court: retained concrete with repaired joints
- Learning Terrace: broom-finished concrete
- Grove: wood-chip mulch around planted beds
- Open Lawn: retained turf
- Water Court: permeable concrete over open-graded aggregate
- Circulation: retained concrete with flush transitions

# ALDER YARD site records

- Y axis: north

## Existing trees

- Tree protection circles: retained soil surface and mulch
- Existing crowns: 4 m diameter; crown base 2,200 mm; tree height 7,000 mm
- New CA stock: two trees; height 3,500 mm; crown diameter 1,500 mm
- Shade-study tree geometry: existing crown dimensions and new stock dimensions above
- New MT stock: 24 shrubs in 5 L containers
- New CD stock: 120 groundcover plants in 2 L containers

## Zone program
| Zone | Area | Capacity | Surface | Shade approach |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Assembly Court | 120 m² | 60 standing pupils | Retained concrete with repaired joints | Overhead canopy |
| Learning Terrace | 120 m² | 30 pupils + 1 teacher | Broom-finished concrete | Canopy edge and tree shade |
| Grove | 180 m² | 12 seated pupils | Wood-chip mulch around planted beds | Four retained and two new CA trees |
| Open Lawn | 140 m² | 30 active pupils | Retained turf | Open sky |
| Water Court | 120 m² | 12 pupils observing infiltration | Permeable concrete over open-graded aggregate | Intermittent tree shade |
| Circulation | 328 m² | Moving pupils and staff | Retained concrete with flush transitions | Mixed sun and shade |

- Landscape area total: 1,008 m²
- Grove location: western courtyard, containing T1-T4
- Learning Terrace location: east of Assembly Court, south of D1
- Water Court location: southeast courtyard, west of maintenance passage
- Circulation area: connecting routes and east maintenance passage

## Sun-study inputs
| Date | Time | Solar azimuth clockwise from north | Solar altitude |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 15 July | 09:30 | 110 degrees | 38 degrees |
| 15 July | 12:30 | 190 degrees | 72 degrees |

## School operations
| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Pupil age range | 8-12 years |
| Lesson state | 09:30; 30 pupils and 1 teacher at Learning Terrace |
| Break state | 12:30; 30 pupils at Assembly Court and 30 at Open Lawn |
| Teaching activities | Group reading, drawing and plant observation |
| Route | D1 to Learning Terrace; maximum walking distance 35 m; minimum clear width 1.8 m |
| Maintenance access | East passage; weekdays 07:00-08:00 |
| Maintenance staffing | Two grounds staff; combined 4 hours per week |
| Establishment irrigation | Drip irrigation to new planting during the first two summers |
| Furniture | Six five-pupil tables, one teacher position, 12 Grove seats |
| Surface maintenance | Weekly litter collection and sweeping; permeable concrete vacuumed twice yearly |

steps.userMessage:
ALDER YARD | Shade and outdoor learning for a school courtyard

Our school needs a courtyard that can support a lesson and remain useful when the bell releases pupils outside. The site is 40 m east–west by 30 m north–south, totaling 1,200 m². The existing north-side school building occupies 192 m²; the landscape area is 1,008 m². Retain its footprint, cream brickwork, teal window frames and four existing Celtis australis trees. Ground level rises 300 mm from south to north. The east-edge maintenance passage stays 4 m wide.

Work from the fixed Assembly Court boundary and the six zone areas in the site records. A class comprises 30 pupils and one teacher; Learning Terrace needs six five-pupil tables and one teacher position, reached from door D1 along a route no longer than 35 m and at least 1.8 m wide. Provide at least 90 m² of geometric shade within the 120 m² Assembly Court at 12:30 on 15 July. Combine a planted grove, shrub and groundcover layers, and an overhead canopy; retain an open lawn and provide 120 m² of permeable concrete. The canopy envelope is 12 m by 10 m, with 3,000 mm minimum clear height and 4,500 mm maximum overall height. Print "ALDER YARD", all six zone names and all three plant names on the masterplan and materials and planting schedule. Use "Geometric shade study" as the shade drawing title.

Audience: pupils and teachers using the courtyard during lessons and breaks, with the school leadership and grounds team choosing the layout and maintenance approach.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the project facts and fixed wording. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. 03-site-records.en.md contains coordinates, tree records, zone areas, sun-study inputs and school operating conditions. school-survey.png supplies the fixed building, trees, assembly boundary, levels and maintenance passage. canopy-envelope.png supplies the canopy span and height limits. existing-schoolyard.png supplies the recognizable building appearance and existing hard court. lesson-atmosphere.png supplies the outdoor teaching context. break-atmosphere.png supplies the lunchtime movement and social context.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page site analysis and zone area table covering all six zones, their areas, surfaces, shade methods, capacities and the three plant names
2. One courtyard masterplan with north arrow, scale bar, boundaries, building, numbered trees, six zones, canopy, planting, furniture and permeable concrete
3. One geometric shade drawing with paired 09:30 and 12:30 plans for 15 July, sun directions, canopy and tree shadows, and shaded Assembly Court areas
4. One section along A–A through Grove, Assembly Court and the eastern courtyard, with tree, shrub and groundcover layers, canopy heights and ground levels
5. One Learning Terrace detail sheet with six five-pupil tables, one teacher position, seating dimensions and the arrival space
6. One planting and facilities plan locating the six trees, 24 shrubs, 120 groundcover plants, furniture and maintenance access
7. One materials and planting schedule repeating the site name, six zone names and areas, plant names and quantities, and surface construction descriptions
8. One circulation and activity diagram comparing a 31-person lesson with a 60-pupil break, including the D1 route length and clear widths
9. Four courtyard perspectives: two fixed viewpoints, each shown during the 09:30 lesson and the 12:30 break
10. One 10-second video moving from D1 to Learning Terrace and ending with an overview of the canopy and Grove
11. One presentation document of at least eight pages reusing the site analysis, masterplan, shade drawing, section, schedule and four perspectives

Acceptance:
- Preserve the 40 m by 30 m boundary, 192 m² building footprint, T1–T4 coordinates and 1.8 m tree protection radii on the masterplan, planting and facilities plan, and circulation diagram; dimension the 4 m maintenance passage and 1.8 m minimum learning route on these drawings.
- Repeat the site analysis areas on the masterplan, materials and planting schedule, and presentation: Assembly Court 120 m², Learning Terrace 120 m², Grove 180 m², Open Lawn 140 m², Water Court 120 m² and Circulation 328 m². Print ALDER YARD and all six zone names on the masterplan, schedule and presentation.
- Repeat Celtis australis, Myrtus communis 'Tarentina' and Carex divulsa from the site analysis on the masterplan, materials and planting schedule, and presentation. Match codes CA, MT and CD between the planting and facilities plan and schedule, with four retained and two new trees, 24 shrubs and 120 groundcover plants; identify Water Court's 120 m² of permeable concrete on the masterplan and schedule.
- Title the shade drawing Geometric shade study, use both supplied sun positions, and label its Assembly Court shadow areas, including at least 90 m² at 12:30. Dimension the 12 m by 10 m canopy envelope on the masterplan and its minimum 3,000 mm clearance and maximum 4,500 mm height on the section; show the grove layers on both drawings.
- Accommodate 30 pupils and one teacher in the Learning Terrace detail, circulation diagram and lesson perspectives. Label the D1 route at 35 m or less on the circulation diagram; distribute the 60-pupil break between Assembly Court and Open Lawn in the diagram and break perspectives, preserving the marked passage widths.
- Match the masterplan's canopy, planting and furniture across both viewpoint pairs, the 10-second video and presentation. Label each perspective with 09:30 lesson or 12:30 break, and repeat the six zone areas and the 90 m² noon shade target in the presentation's minimum eight pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
